lessons.claim: Using Hangul in a result figure breaks the font **from both sides**. matplotlib's default DejaVu Sans has no Hangul glyphs so the labels all become □, and conversely the Hangul fonts have no symbols -- measured, AppleGothic · Apple SD Gothic Neo · NanumGothic, **all three**, lack U+2212 (−) and ŷ (U+0177). The only one on macOS with both Hangul and the symbols was **Arial Unicode MS** (confirmed by querying the cmap directly with fontTools). ★ rcParams['axes.unicode_minus']=False fixes **only the tick labels** and the − in a string literal still breaks. After generating, it has to be confirmed that the 'missing from font' / 'does not have a glyph' warnings on stderr are 0 -- ignore a warning and you end up presenting as a result a picture a human cannot read. ffmpeg is not in this environment so animations are written with PillowWriter (GIF).
